Strategic Vision

Re-architecting Product Marketing for the AI Era

How SAP PMM connects product and go-to-market at scale — bringing people, process, and technology together to operationalize the Book of Work and deliver AI-enabled execution.

By Chris O'Hara & Sean Thomson · October 2026 · 12 min read

Three shifts are converging at once — and product marketing needs a new operating model to respond.

First: we now have a common definition of PMM responsibilities. The Book of Work creates shared standards and interlocks across SAP. For the first time, we can articulate what great PMM execution looks like — consistently, across every line of business.

Second: AI at scale. Tools, pilots, and LoB innovation are accelerating faster than our ability to coordinate them. The value of AI depends on repeatable workflows, governance, and adoption — not just experimentation. We need to standardize before we automate.

Third: organizational change. Shifts in how we're structured raise the stakes on shared learning, reusable practices, and visibility across lines of business. We need to connect what works and scale it.

This article lays out how we're responding — the Northstar, the economic model, the architecture, and the roadmap.

The Northstar: 10x PMM

Here's the vision in one sentence: Common standards and AI cut the effort of repeatable work, so PMM capacity shifts to strategy, insight, and growth.

We call this the 10x PMM — not because we're asking people to work ten times harder, but because the combination of clear standards, AI-enabled execution, and connected learning can multiply what each PMM accomplishes.

📘

Book of Work

Defines the standard. Embed best practice. Reduce reinvention. Measure impact.

🤖

Transforms the execution. Automate repeatable work. Embed standards. Unlock productivity.

These three pillars — standards, AI, and community — reinforce each other. The Book of Work tells us what great looks like. AI workflows help us do it faster. NextGen PMM helps us learn together. None of them works in isolation; all three need to develop in parallel.

The 10x PMM Promise

More revenue. More capacity. Lower cost to scale.

Three Priorities

Strategy without focus is noise. We've distilled the work into three priorities that guide everything else:

1. Enable Our PMMs

Build AI capability into priority Book of Work workflows through learning, playbooks, and LoB champions. The goal: AI becomes part of everyday PMM execution — not a separate initiative, but the way work gets done.

2. Define Our Toolset & Drive Adoption

Identify the approved AI tools and capabilities PMMs need. Reduce fragmentation and duplicate experimentation. Give people clarity about what to use, when to use it, and how to get started. The right tools for the right PMM workflows.

3. Embed PMM Intelligence into SAP AI

Bring trusted PMM knowledge, standards, and messaging into SAP AI tools — Joule Work Desktop, EKX, Customer Strategy Explorer, and future AI experiences. The goal: PMM expertise becomes reusable enterprise intelligence.

PMM as the Trusted Source

Here's the big idea: PMM-approved messaging should be authoritative, current, reusable, and consistent across SAP's AI experiences.

We create and govern the narrative once — positioning, messaging, value propositions, differentiation, competitive intelligence, use cases — then make it consumable by SAP AI.

EKX (trusted enterprise knowledge & retrieval) ensures approved PMM positioning, messaging, differentiation, and product knowledge are authoritative and discoverable. PMM content becomes trusted knowledge.

Customer Strategy Explorer brings approved value propositions, personas, use cases, and differentiation into customer-specific recommendations. PMM content becomes customer relevance.

Joule Work Desktop makes trusted PMM knowledge available to Joule Skills, agents, and everyday workflows. PMM content becomes execution at scale.

The PMM AI Harness

Think of it as three layers working together:

Standards

The PMM Book of Work defines how great PMM work gets done — methods, positioning, GTM standards.

Reusable Skills

The CMO Skill Library turns best practices into reusable AI-powered workflows. Messaging PoC first, then CI, launch, sales plays, demand.

Content & Trust

The Trusted Business Context grounds every skill in approved, current intelligence — brand, LoB messaging, product, CI, proof points.

The harness sits underneath everything. Governance controls how AI reaches it. Trusted PMM content shows up wherever work gets done — EKX, Customer Strategy Explorer, Joule Work Desktop, even approved third-party tools.

The Pilot Proved the Model

We didn't build this strategy in a vacuum. The NextGen PMM pilot — a 12-unit curriculum plus live AI Labs, mapped directly to the Book of Work — validated the approach with real PMMs, on real work.

181
PMMs Enrolled
73%
Quiz Pass Rate
9.1
NPS Score (0–10)

The numbers matter, but the qualitative feedback matters more:

  • The mindset shifted. PMMs moved from treating AI as a tool to working with AI as a co-worker.
  • 4.2 / 5 overall value rating. Content, Labs, and assessments all scored between 4.1 and 4.3. 85% found the level just right.
  • 60%+ are already applying it at work. This isn't theoretical — people are using what they learned.

The pilot proves the model. AI as co-worker, mapped to the Book of Work, validated by practitioners. We're ready to move from pilot to SAP-wide launch.

The Collaboration Model

Local LoB innovation becomes shared PMM capability. Enterprise governance sets the guardrails. Lines of business innovate. The PMM AI Council decides what should scale.

The model has three layers:

  • Core Team — Orchestrate the PMM AI portfolio, interface with the Global Marketing AI Council, identify duplication, connect teams solving similar problems.
  • LoB AI Champions — Represent their LoB in the PMM AI Council, surface local innovation, validate shared capabilities, drive adoption within their teams.
  • Workflow AI Leads — Own a core PMM workflow across LoBs, develop and validate specific AI use cases end to end, codify reusable playbooks.

Every LoB has a voice. Every priority workflow has an owner. The PMM AI Council connects the two.

The Roadmap

Four phases through the remainder of 2026, leading to launch at MKOM 2027:

Path to Launch

Sept / Oct
Build the foundation. Migrate to SAP BTP. Redesign around the Book of Work. Align the PMM Learning Journey. Validate priority Writer and Crayon use cases.
November
Pilot & validate. Beta with PMM AI Champions. Test priority AI workflows. Validate usability, relevance, and value. Gather lighthouse PMM feedback.
December
Prepare to scale. Refine the experience from pilot feedback. Finalize core Book of Work content. Activate PMM Champions. Prepare launch communications and enablement.
January
Launch & activate. Launch at MKOM 2027. Activate the PMM Community and champions. Measure reach, adoption, capability, and impact. Integrate productivity into 2027 PMM KPIs.

After launch, we evolve and grow: expand priority AI workflows, scale proven capabilities across LoBs, measure productivity and business impact, and continuously refresh learning, best practices, and AI capabilities.

What This Means for You

If you're a PMM at SAP, here's what to expect:

  • One front door — NextGen PMM becomes the home for Product Marketing. Know the work, build the skills, execute with AI.
  • Clear standards — The Book of Work tells you what great looks like. No more guessing.
  • AI in the flow of work — Approved tools, agents, prompts, and guided workflows — embedded where you already work.
  • Connected community — Champions in every LoB. Shared learning. Practices that scale.

This isn't a mandate. It's an invitation. The people who engage early — who experiment, who share what they learn, who help shape the tools and workflows — will define what PMM looks like at SAP for the next decade.

The model is proven. The sponsorship is real. The people are in place.
